subject: Rerank qualification & validation playbook — post-call next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Chatterjee <priya@shopline-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed rerank validation playbook

Hi Priya / Daniel — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the evaluation.

Call recap (5 bullets):
- Problem: Shopline wants to reorder search and recommendations to increase relevance for commerce queries while avoiding regression on long-tail SKUs.
- Current baseline: production ranking is a heuristic + BM25 hybrid; you supplied a sample of 120k query-item interactions for preliminary analysis.
- Success metrics you care about: NDCG@5/10, MRR, and a business metric — 7-day conversion delta for served query sessions.
- Risk flags: potential distribution shift for seasonal SKUs and cold-start items; latency SLO of 120ms p95 for rerank endpoint.
- Timeline: 2-week local evaluation, then a 2-week A/B canary.

Recommended evaluation plan (proposal):
1) Offline bench (this week): run NDCG/MRR + per-query bucket breakdowns on the sample dataset. Models we recommend to benchmark:
   - redwood-rerank-1 (quantized fp16/8 hybrid) — strong latency/cost profile
   - mistral-re-rank-v1 (full-fp16) — higher quality on paraphrase-heavy queries in our tests
   - llama3-rerank-16b (baseline comparison)
2) Prompt sets & templates: we suggest the enclosed prompt_sets_v1.json (includes brand-aware templates and negative-sampling rules).
3) Instrumentation: we need a small server-side flag for 50/50 split and logging of session ids + click/conversion events.
4) Canary A/B: 50/50 (two weeks) with daily early-warning checks for NDCG dips > 1.5 points or conversion drop > 2%.

Deliverables we will share by EOD Thursday:
- Full offline eval (NDCG@5/10, MRR) + per-query buckets (head/tail/seasonal). (attachment: rerank_eval_notebook.ipynb)
- Notebook with code + instructions to reproduce locally + Drive links to prompts.

Ask from your side: please attach the canonical label file (clicks/ctr conversions) and the schema for event logs (we received the 120k sample but need session ids and timestamps).

I've attached a quick starter notebook and the prompt set. If you confirm the instrumentation owner and the event schema, we can start the offline runs tomorrow.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
--

Thanks Jonas — recap looks good and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick items: 

1) Labels: attaching the latest sample labels (shopline_sample_labels.csv) — includes session_id, query, candidate_ids, clicked_item_id, timestamp. The full set has PII redacted.
2) Baseline numbers: our in-house team reports current NDCG@10 = 0.612 and MRR = 0.43 on the sample slice we shared.
3) Instrumentation: Daniel will own the server-side flag and will loop in infra; I can coordinate with product for event export. Can you confirm what logs Redwood requires for the session-level conversion delta?

Question: on the offline run — will Redwood compute per-query difficulty buckets (e.g., frequent/rare/paraphrase)? We want a clear breakdown so we can judge quality regressions.

We'll review the notebook today and confirm whether the session ids are sufficient. Thanks — Priya

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Chatterjee <priya@shopline-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed rerank validation playbook

Great — thanks for the baseline and the labels. A few clarifications and a preview of the offline results (quick summary from today's initial run):

What we need from instrumentation (minimal):
- event logs with session_id, served_rank, click_flag, purchase_flag, timestamp, and a stable user/session id.
- flag endpoint for 50/50 split + ability to route by customer or route.

Initial offline comparisons (on the 120k sample; held-out 10%):
- production-baseline (heuristic+BM25): NDCG@10 = 0.612, MRR = 0.430
- redwood-rerank-1 (quantized): NDCG@10 = 0.684, MRR = 0.512
- mistral-re-rank-v1: NDCG@10 = 0.699, MRR = 0.525
- llama3-rerank-16b: NDCG@10 = 0.671, MRR = 0.498

Key observations:
- Mistral shows a small lead (~0.015 NDCG) vs redwood-rerank-1 but at ~20% higher p95 latency in our local infra.
- redwood-rerank-1 has a better cost/latency tradeoff and is within 1% of Mistral on commercial queries (high-traffic buckets).
- Tail queries (bottom 25% frequency) show more variance; Mistral improves those by ~2–3 NDCG points but also introduces a small number of harmful rewrites for product titles in a hand-inspected sample. This is the quality-regression risk we highlighted in the call.

Proposed A/B plan (concrete):
- Phase 1 (Offline): finalize prompt sets and run full-eval + per-bucket delta. Deliverable by Fri EOD.
- Phase 2 (Canary A/B): 50/50, 2 weeks, daily monitoring for NDCG@5/10, MRR, latency p95, and business conversion delta. Early-warning thresholds: NDCG drop > 1.5 pts or conversion drop > 2%.
- Phase 3 (Rollout): if >= 1.5 pt NDCG uplift on primary buckets and no conversion regression, expand to 100% with staged ramp.

Instrumentation owner: Daniel (per your note). Marissa / Karthik — can Redwood help instrument the logging webhook or do you want us to provide the logging schema? We can also push a small client library to capture stable session ids.

Attachments/links: rerank_eval_notebook.ipynb (contains the scripts, the bucketization logic, and the exact NDCG/MRR calculation). Link to the evaluation run: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/7890

If you agree to the thresholds and timeline, we'll queue the full offline sweep tonight and provide the notebook output tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Jonas

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147
